text:
Ana: Heads-up — Sales just flagged a parity ask. Competitor shipped per-route SLOs + automatic fallback to smaller models when capacity's tight. A customer asked if we can match. Thoughts?

Matt: Do we have the link / exact feature callout? quick summary pls.

Ana: Link sent in DM. TL;DR: per-route latency target + simple toggle in UI, and a fallback chain that shifts to thinner models automatically. Sales says one enterprise was sold on the simplicity.

Rachel: We already support routing policies and model fallbacks, but we don't expose per-route SLOs as a first-class config in the Console/ API. Could be surface-level work vs infra enforcement.

Sam: Options I see: A) Surface a per-route SLO toggle in Console + API flag that maps to existing routing (low effort) B) Implement server-side strict enforcement that throttles/queues and triggers fallbacks (higher infra work + SLA implications) C) push back and frame our differentiators (cost controls, batching) instead of parity.

Kevin: For parity, minimal launch criteria: UI toggle, API param, and metrics (per-route latency/cost) + alerting. If Sales wants a contractual SLA we move to B. Timeline estimate?

Matt: Eng capacity is tight. If we want a quick market response, go for A first (quick win), then iterate toward B if traction demands. Need PM PRD + spike on autoscaling/fallback correctness.

Ana: I'll draft a short PRD (use-case, acceptance criteria, rollout plan). @Sam can you ballpark infra effort for A vs B?

Sam: Ballpark: A = 2 Engs for ~3w (API + Console + metrics plumbing). B = +2 Engs and 4–6w for enforcement, queueing, and SLA metadata work. Big risk for B: cross-model fallback correctness under heavy tail loads.

Rachel: Add acceptance criteria: 1) E2E perf test with synthetic traffic 2) Measured cost delta per-token for typical workloads 3) Fallback correctness tests (no silent degradation) 4) Rollout plan with canary and auto-rollback on errors. Also doc sales play and suggested pricing uplift for SLA.

Matt: +1. Also include an explicit migration path for customers who want hard SLAs later. Note: fallback selection policy should be configurable (latency-first vs cost-first).

Ana: I'll include that. Draft PRD to #product-docs by EOW and drop a short decision doc before product sync.

Sam: example API payload we can expose initially: `{"route_slo_ms":100, "fallback_policy":"model_size"}`

Kevin: I'll reserve a Dedicated capacity slot tentatively if we greenlight enforcement (B).

DeployBot: Reminder — product sync scheduled Fri 10:00. :bell:

Ana: Cool. Please add any other risks or customer asks in the PRD thread. Need a go/no-go at the sync. :calendar:
